order: show the answering model's name at the bottom, with a dot next to it while the agent is working
rationale: The only case that exercises the when-condition arm of the bind validator (validate.go: 'unsigned bind %q in when condition of node type %q'), which reports through the same scene.Error type as a node bind but from a different walk and so can regress independently. That validator coverage is the reason it stays, and it is carried entirely by the attempt: TestEveryExpectedRefusalIsTheRefusalTheEngineGives holds the attempt to reproducing that exact refusal at its address, so the diagnostic cannot rot silently. Measured against a real model (deepseek-v4.1-flash) it converged in one turn, spelling agent.working directly rather than taking the predicted agent.busy miss, so per EVAL.md it measures the first shot and stays only for that validator coverage. The design keeps two nodes deliberately apart: model.name is ungated so it is the must_bind field (a must_bind field has to reach the frame -- TestEveryCorpusMustBindFieldReachesTheFrame renders the convergence document with agent.working=false and requires the value to appear -- and a field hidden behind its own when would never render there), while the working-dot is the node that carries the when, so the unsigned-when refusal is provoked without hiding the content the frame test checks. model.name is novel against RAW, which binds it nowhere, so doing nothing does not pass.

attempts.note: model.name is right, but the working-dot guesses agent.busy in its when; a when is validated against the same signed set as a bind, and BINDS.md signs the boolean as agent.working
